steps.check: exhaustive: 1120 A2 subsystems in E8; one reflection-orbit covers all 1120 (W-transitive)
steps.determines: UNIQUE (1120 A2 subsystems; one W(E8) orbit)
steps.expr: an A2 subsystem = 6 roots {+-a, +-b, +-(a+b)} with <a,b> = -1 (120 degrees); exhaustive over 12's 240 roots gives EXACTLY 1120 such subsystems; a single reflection-orbit (BFS under the 240 root reflections) of ONE A2 reaches all 1120 -> W(E8) transitive. With no extra structure the A2 is maximally undetermined: one Weyl orbit, nothing singled out
steps.what: BASELINE: the A2 subsystems of E8 number EXACTLY 1120 and W(E8) is transitive on them -- computed from 12's 240 roots (the prose-only '1120 checked' now a checked object)
steps.why: the honest baseline, and a needed correction. Containers 31 and 61 CITE 'all A2 subgroups of E8 are Weyl-transitive (1120 checked)' -- but neither COMPUTED it; it lived only in prose (an answer-in-prose, the CORRECTIONS #1 pattern). Here it is derived cold: enumerate every A2 subsystem from 12's roots (1120), and witness transitivity by a single Weyl orbit reaching all 1120. This is the object the embedding-distinction test must cut. Exact-integer over H; the orbit BFS is deterministic.

steps.check: conjugation-by-g3: M^3=I!=M, M H M^T=H, permutes 240 roots; fixed locus 12 roots = A2xA2
steps.determines: UNIQUE (conjugation by g3 is an order-3 E8 isometry; fixed locus = A2 x A2, 12 roots)
steps.expr: Xi = conjugation x -> g3.x.g3^-1 by g3=(-1/2,1/2,1/2,1/2) (31); unit-quaternion conjugation preserves the codifferent form, so M is an ISOMETRY (M H M^T = H), of order 3 (M^3=I != M), permuting the 240 roots. Its FIXED subspace is 4-dimensional and contains EXACTLY 12 roots, whose inner-product signature (12 self, 12 antipodal, 24 at +1, 24 at -1, 72 at 0) is that of A2 x A2 -- two ORTHOGONAL A2's. (Contrast: the Galois involution sigma, phi->1-phi, is order 2 and NOT an isometry of the trace form -- it swaps the two real embeddings -- so 'sigma-fixed A2' is ill-posed; conjugation by g3 is the well-posed, substrate-native Xi.)

value.note: sigma (phi->1-phi) is the two-embedding swap, NOT an E8 isometry -> Xi = conjugation by g3

steps.what: the substrate-native Xi: CONJUGATION by g3 (31's colour element) is an order-3 E8 isometry; its FIXED LOCUS is an A2 x A2 (12 roots, 4-dim). (The Galois sigma is NOT an isometry -- why this Xi.)
steps.why: the choice of Xi, made principled and well-posed. The K2 review doc asked for a substrate-native datum recovered as the FIXED-POINT LOCUS of an intrinsic operator. The obvious candidate -- the Galois involution sigma -- FAILS to be an isometry (checked: it is the two-embedding swap, not a symmetry of E8), so it does not act on the root system and cannot have 'fixed A2's'. The correct Xi is container 31's own colour operator: conjugation by an order-3 element g3 of 2I. Because g3 is a unit, conjugation preserves the quaternion norm and hence the codifferent form (06.6) -- a genuine element of Aut(E8)=W(E8). Cold computation: M^3=I, M!=I, M H M^T = H, M permutes the 240 roots; the fixed space is 4-dimensional with exactly 12 roots in the A2 x A2 signature. So the substrate's colour-Z/3 has a real, 4-dimensional fixed root-subsystem inside E8 -- the object ED.3 tests against the 1120.

steps.check: g3 on the 1120 A2's: 4 invariant (2 fixed + 2 triality) + 372 three-cycles = 4+3*372=1120
steps.determines: UNIQUE (4 invariant A2's = 2 fixed + 2 triality; 372 three-cycles; 4+3*372=1120)
steps.expr: acting on the 1120 A2 subsystems, conjugation-by-g3 leaves EXACTLY 4 setwise-invariant: 2 are pointwise-FIXED (the two orthogonal A2's of the ED.2 fixed A2 x A2) and 2 are TRIALITY A2's -- g3 acts on each as cycle-type [3,3], cyclically permuting its 3 positive roots (and its 3 negatives): g3 IS the A2 centre / the colour-Z/3 seating (exactly 31's 'three seatings' realized inside an E8 A2). The remaining 1116 A2's fall into 372 three-cycles (4 + 3*372 = 1120). So Xi CUTS the Weyl-transitive 1120 down to a distinguished handful. It does NOT isolate a unique A2 (no forcing); it does NOT leave them fully arbitrary (the cut is real and substrate-native)

value.reading: g3 cuts 1120 -> an A2xA2 (fixed) + 2 triality A2's; not a unique A2

steps.what: THE CUT: conjugation-by-g3 leaves EXACTLY 4 of the 1120 A2's invariant -- 2 pointwise-FIXED (the A2xA2 components) + 2 TRIALITY (g3 cycles their 3 roots) -- the other 1116 in 372 three-cycles. A real cut, not a unique A2
steps.why: the discriminating result -- neither dismissal nor forcing. Against the null hypothesis (the A2 is one undifferentiated W-orbit of 1120, ED.1), the substrate's OWN colour operator is NOT inert: it fixes an A2 x A2 and, more tellingly, acts as exact TRIALITY on two further A2's -- meaning g3 plays the role of the SU(3) centre on them, the group-theoretic content of 'colour = three seatings' (31) seen directly inside E8. That is a genuine reduction of the 1120. But it is a cut to a HANDFUL (an A2xA2 + 2 triality A2's), not a selection of one A2 -- so it forces nothing, and ED.4 shows even this handful is not canonical. G4 refuter: had g3 left all 1120 in free 3-cycles (no invariant A2), Xi would be inert and the arbitrary verdict (option 1) would stand cold; it does not. G3: the computation never names 'colour' or 'family' -- it is g3's action on root subsystems.

steps.check: 20 order-3 elements (one 2I-class); 10 A2xA2 loci; all 2I-conjugate -> axis unforced
steps.determines: UNIQUE (20 order-3 elements = one 2I-class; 10 A2xA2 loci; all 2I-conjugate)
steps.expr: the order-3 elements of 2I are EXACTLY 20 and form a SINGLE 2I-conjugacy class (conjugating g3 by the 120 icosians yields all 20 -- 31's class of 20). They give 10 distinct A2 x A2 fixed-loci (g3 and g3^-1=g3^2 share a locus, 20/2=10), and all 10 lie in ONE orbit under the inner-automorphism isometries (conjugation by the 120 icosians) -- hence W(E8)-conjugate. So the distinguished A2 x A2 is determined only up to the CHOICE of order-3 colour axis, and that choice is itself substrate-unforced (all 20 conjugate). The arbitrariness is RELOCATED to 'which colour axis', not removed

value.reading: distinguished A2xA2 is canonical only up to the colour axis, itself unforced

steps.what: NON-CANONICITY: g3 is one of EXACTLY 20 order-3 elements (a single 2I-conjugacy class), giving 10 distinct A2xA2 loci, ALL 2I-conjugate -- so the distinguished A2xA2 is fixed only UP TO the colour axis, itself unforced
steps.why: the honest residual -- and it is the crux of the verdict. The cut of ED.3 is real, but is it canonical? No. The substrate has no distinguished order-3 element: the 20 are one conjugacy class (31), and their fixed A2 x A2's are all conjugate (checked: one 2I-orbit covers all 10 loci). So choosing g3 and thereby its A2 x A2 is exactly as unforced as choosing a colour axis -- which is physically apt: colour SU(3) has no canonical embedding either (31 already makes 'colour' basis-/conjugacy-dependent). The embedding-distinction is therefore a REDUCTION -- 'which A2' collapses to 'which order-3 element' -- not an elimination to a unique object. This is precisely the twin of 61's count-3: there 'which count' reduced to 'the outer Z/3'; here 'which A2' reduces to 'the native order-3 conjugation'.

steps.determines: POSTULATE (embedding-distinction reduces to the native order-3 axis: eliminative (opt 2) + residual arbitrary (opt 1); not forced)
steps.expr: the disciplined verdict of the embedding-distinction test. The substrate-native Xi (conjugation by an order-3 element, 31's colour operator) is NOT inert against the Weyl-transitive 1120 A2's: it cuts them to a distinguished A2 x A2 (its fixed locus) plus two triality A2's where g3 IS the colour centre (ED.2/ED.3). But it forces no unique A2, and the cut is canonical only up to the choice of order-3 colour axis, which is itself unforced (ED.4: 20 elements, one class, 10 conjugate loci). Mapping to Kevin's three options: this is OPTION (2) -- we ELIMINATE (1120 -> an A2xA2 + triality A2's) but cannot derive a UNIQUE one -- with the residual choice OPTION (1) [the colour axis is arbitrary]. It is NOT option (3): no perceived mechanism forces a canonical axis here. Whether a DEEPER substrate structure canonicalizes the axis (option 3 -- possibly a separate research program, or a later-discovery) is OPEN. So the embedding-distinction is a genuine REDUCTION ('which A2' -> 'which native order-3 element'), structurally identical to 61's count-3 reduction -- partly structured (a real, substrate-native cut), unforced (no unique A2; axis arbitrary). NOT a root, NOT solved, NOT refuted
